what: Kinder Morgan owns energy infrastructure: about 66,000 miles of natural gas pipelines, terminals that store fuels and chemicals, and carbon dioxide used for enhanced oil recovery.
customers: Utilities and power producers, gas producers, refiners, liquefied natural gas exporters and chemical companies.
money: transporting and storing gas under long-term capacity contracts
storing and moving refined fuels, chemicals and crude
carbon dioxide supply and enhanced oil recovery
moat: Pipeline corridors and permits that would be nearly impossible to obtain today, with revenue mostly from reserved capacity rather than volumes.
risks: Debt of about $33 billion is large relative to earnings
New pipeline projects face long permitting and legal battles
Returns on capital are modest at around 6%
Refined product volumes face long-term pressure from electric vehicles
opportunities: Gas demand from data centre power plants and liquefied natural gas exports is rising
About two-thirds of earnings come from take-or-pay style contracts
A dividend yield near 4% is covered by stable contracted cash flow
watch: New project backlog and the share of earnings under fixed-fee contracts.
